title: gp channel — schema-first (AFB backend<->AFB frontend only; not part of afb.execution.v1 wire)
description: Negotiated via auth.support/auth_ok.support (capability id afbws.gp.channel.v2). Items are afb.gp.v2 (`instrument_key`, kinds trendline/fibonacci; primitive parameters `start`/`stop`/`text` live in the `settings` dictionary, strictly typed by `kind`). Same convention as afbws.market: ONE schema id per message (`afbws.gp.<op>.v2`, no .request/.response/.push suffixes); the same schema is the request, its response and, where documented, a server push. Requests and responses are told apart by direction and fields (a response echoes the request's `request_id`); a message WITHOUT `request_id` is a server push. Collections are always arrays (`items[]`, `ids[]`, `instrument_keys[]`), so bulk operations are single messages; partial failures come back in `rejected[]`. Chart-indicator management (replaces legacy settings/{get,set,get_default,set_default} `indicators`) is `indicator.list|set|delete`; shared indicators are changed by a manager only and pushed to everyone via `indicator.set`/`indicator.delete` without `request_id`. Chart datasets (primary-data series staff made available: a field of the market.v2 registry or the candles, with a name and a default style; `scope: personal` is a staff draft, `shared` is published) are `dataset.list|set|delete` — read by everyone (a regular user sees shared ones only), written and deleted by staff only; changes of shared datasets are pushed without `request_id`. Chart presets (datasets laid out on the price/upper/lower panes with per-item style overrides) are `preset.list|set|delete`, with the same rules (shared presets are written and deleted by staff only and reference shared datasets only; changes of shared presets are pushed without `request_id`). Primitive display settings: `style`. See AFB/docs/ENTITY_WS_PROTOCOL.md.

list.title: afbws.gp.list.v2 — read primitives (client -> server request, server -> client response).
list.description: Request: optional filters `ids[]` and/or `instrument_keys[]` (both given = intersection; none = every primitive the caller owns). Response: same `request_id`, `items[]` (afb.gp.v2) — possibly empty, never an error for a missing id. There is no separate `get`: use `ids`. `items` is response-only; a request carrying `items` together with a filter is invalid.

set.title: afbws.gp.set.v2 — upsert primitives (request / response / server push).
set.description: Request (`request_id` present, `items` = what the client wants stored): upsert by `item.id`, batched (each item carries `settings`; `settings` is replaced as a whole; a client-sent `tradeplan_id` is ignored in favour of the stored one); moving a primitive is the same request as creating or editing one. Response (same `request_id`): `items` = the authoritative stored records that were applied (possibly empty), `rejected[]` = items that were NOT applied, each with a typed reason (partial failure never fails the whole message; the backend alone decides whether a move is safe against linked tradeplans). Push (no `request_id`, server-initiated): ownership delta by id — `items[]` are authoritative afb.gp.v2 records (bind: `tradeplan_id` set on publish/amend; release: `tradeplan_id` cleared on plan physical delete); never a snapshot, `rejected` is not allowed. Primitive removal is conveyed by `afbws.gp.delete.v2` without `request_id`.

delete.title: afbws.gp.delete.v2 — delete primitives (request / response / server push).
delete.description: Request (`request_id` present): `ids[]` and/or `instrument_keys[]` (at least one; `instrument_keys` = every FREE primitive of those instruments in one call). Primitives owned by a tradeplan (`tradeplan_id`) are never removed here — they come back in `rejected[]` with `code: conflict` and `details` (linked plans/deals). Response (same `request_id`): `ids[]` = ids actually removed (possibly empty), `rejected[]`. Push (no `request_id`): `ids[]` removed by the server; `instrument_keys`/`rejected` are not allowed.

rejection.title: One primitive that was not applied by set/delete.
rejection.description: `item` carries the authoritative current record when the client should see it (a rejected move restores the server's version, not the client's optimistic one). `details` is populated on `conflict` (linked tradeplans/deals, locked scopes).

indicatorList.title: afbws.gp.indicator.list.v2 — read chart indicators (request / response).
indicatorList.description: Request: only `request_id`. Response (same `request_id`): `items[]` — the caller's merged list (shared + personal).

indicatorSet.title: afbws.gp.indicator.set.v2 — upsert chart indicators (request / response / server push).
indicatorSet.description: Request: upsert by `id`, batched. Personal indicators for everyone; `scope: shared` only for a manager (otherwise that item is rejected with `forbidden`). Response (same `request_id`): applied `items[]` (possibly empty) + `rejected[]`. Push (no `request_id`): changed SHARED indicators to every connection with this capability (full authoritative records); personal ones are never pushed. Whether an indicator is drawn on the chart is NOT part of the protocol — it is a per-device view setting kept in the client's localStorage.

indicatorDelete.title: afbws.gp.indicator.delete.v2 — delete chart indicators (request / response / server push).
indicatorDelete.description: Request: `ids[]` (shared ones: manager only, otherwise rejected with `forbidden`; unknown id: `not_found`). Response (same `request_id`): `ids[]` actually removed + `rejected[]`. Push (no `request_id`): shared indicators deleted by a manager (`ids[]`, `rejected` not allowed).

indicatorRejection.title: One indicator that was not applied by indicator.set/indicator.delete.

datasetList.title: afbws.gp.dataset.list.v2 — read chart datasets (request / response).
datasetList.description: Request: only `request_id`. Response (same `request_id`): `items[]` — staff get the shared datasets plus their own personal drafts (`scope: personal`), a regular user gets the shared datasets only.

datasetSet.title: afbws.gp.dataset.set.v2 — upsert chart datasets (request / response / server push).
datasetSet.description: Request: upsert by `id`, batched; STAFF ONLY — a regular user gets every item rejected with `forbidden`. `scope: personal` is a draft visible to its author only, `scope: shared` publishes the dataset to everyone. Validation per item (violation = rejected with `validation_error`): `field` must exist in the registry (and `@window(N)` match the field's `window` flag and 2..`window_max_bars`); `style` must be COMPLETE and its shape must fit the kind of the series (candles: `candleStyle` — `chartType`/`upColor`/`downColor`/`volumeUpColor`/`volumeDownColor`; others: `seriesStyle` — `seriesType`/`color`/`lineWidth`/`lineStyle`) — the schema itself accepts either shape for any field; `unit` in the request is ignored, the server fills it. Response (same `request_id`): applied `items[]` (possibly empty, with `unit` filled) + `rejected[]`. Push (no `request_id`): changed SHARED datasets to every connection with this capability (full authoritative records); personal drafts are never pushed.

datasetDelete.title: afbws.gp.dataset.delete.v2 — delete chart datasets (request / response / server push).
datasetDelete.description: Request: `ids[]`; STAFF ONLY (a regular user gets `forbidden` per id; unknown id: `not_found`; a dataset still referenced by a preset may be refused with `conflict`, as decided by the server). Response (same `request_id`): `ids[]` actually removed + `rejected[]`. Push (no `request_id`): shared datasets deleted by staff (`ids[]`, `rejected` not allowed).

presetList.title: afbws.gp.preset.list.v2 — read chart presets (request / response).
presetList.description: Request: only `request_id`. Response (same `request_id`): `items[]` — the caller's merged list (shared + personal).

presetSet.title: afbws.gp.preset.set.v2 — upsert chart presets (request / response / server push).
presetSet.description: Request: upsert by `id`, batched. Personal presets for everyone; `scope: shared` only for staff (otherwise that item is rejected with `forbidden`). Validation per item (violation = rejected with `validation_error`) — the pane rules of `$defs/preset` in gp.v2.json: every referenced dataset (`panes.*[].dataset`) must exist and be visible to the author; a shared preset may reference shared datasets only; `price` takes only datasets of price scale class; `candles` only on `price`, at most once; one scale class per `upper`/`lower` pane; a dataset must not repeat in a preset; item `style` holds only overrides valid for the dataset's kind. Response (same `request_id`): applied `items[]` (possibly empty) + `rejected[]`. Push (no `request_id`): changed SHARED presets to every connection with this capability (full authoritative records); personal ones are never pushed.

presetDelete.title: afbws.gp.preset.delete.v2 — delete chart presets (request / response / server push).
presetDelete.description: Request: `ids[]` (shared ones: staff only, otherwise rejected with `forbidden`; unknown id: `not_found`). Response (same `request_id`): `ids[]` actually removed + `rejected[]`. Push (no `request_id`): shared presets deleted by staff (`ids[]`, `rejected` not allowed).

presetRejection.title: One preset that was not applied by preset.set/preset.delete.

style.title: afbws.gp.style.v2 — primitive display settings (request / response / server push).
style.description: Per-user chart styling of primitives by kind (replaces the legacy `settings.interface.primitive_styles`). Request without `styles` = read. Request with `styles` = write: it creates or replaces the caller's PERSONAL rows for the supplied kinds, kinds not supplied are left as they are. Response (same `request_id`) and push always carry the EFFECTIVE set — every seeded kind with the caller's personal style if there is one, otherwise the shared one. Push (no `request_id`) delivers that set to the user's other connections after a write; `styles` is required there. Each style is a complete `lineObjectStyle` (colour `#rrggbbaa`).

error.title: afbws.gp.error.v2 — typed error for a whole request (server -> client).
error.description: Used when the request as a whole fails (invalid_schema, forbidden channel, internal_error, ...). Per-item failures of a batched set/delete/indicator.* are reported in that response's `rejected[]`, not here. `details` is populated on `conflict`.

errorDetails.title: Which linked tradeplans/deals blocked a delete/move, and which scopes are locked — populated on `conflict`.
